text:
Sims Elementary reports 26 white students enrolled for 2024-25
For the 2024-25 school year, Sims Elementary School registered an enrollment of 26 white students, a rise of 18.2% compared to the prior year, based on reports from the Georgia Department of Education.
The school’s total student body reached 436 in 2024-25, with white students comprising 6%—making them the third-largest demographic group at Sims Elementary.
Located within Rockdale County School District, Sims Elementary operates in a district headquartered in Conyers.
Of the 18 schools in the Rockdale County School District, Heritage High School had the single highest white student enrollment, reporting 138 white students for the 2024-25 school year.
Statewide, Georgia's public schools enrolled more than 1.7 million students, according to the Georgia Department of Education's Fiscal Year 2026-1 report. Elementary grades enrolled 787,206 students (45.9%), while middle schools reported 388,733 (22.7%), and high schools had 539,092 (31.4%).
Chronic absenteeism persists as a issue for Georgia schools after the pandemic, with 20.7% of students missing 10% or more school days in 2024, the Georgia Department of Education reported. GaDOE responded with a statewide campaign featuring a real-time attendance dashboard, awareness outreach, and targeted district resources to encourage regular attendance.
In 2025, Georgia legislators updated state school attendance laws to prohibit expulsion solely for absenteeism, require additional reporting, and coordinate programs offering alternative diploma pathways.
By 2026, Georgia’s average student-to-teacher ratio was about 14:1, an improvement compared to the national average of 15:1.
